prompt: A news site tests 6 headlines per article and wants to send most readers to the best one while it's still learning which that is.
tells: send most readers to the best one while it's still learning
why: Bandits (Thompson sampling, UCB) shift traffic toward winners as evidence arrives.
trap: A fixed A/B split keeps wasting traffic on losing headlines.

prompt: A promotion runs for only 48 hours, so there's no time to finish a test and then roll out the winner.
tells: no time to finish a test and then roll out
why: Exploit while exploring: maximize total conversions during the window.
trap: Test-then-launch fits long-lived changes, not short windows.

prompt: The goal is to minimize lost revenue from showing worse variants during the experiment, not to measure each variant precisely.
tells: minimize lost revenue from showing worse variants
not to measure each variant precisely
why: Minimizing regret is exactly what bandit algorithms optimize.
trap: A/B tests prioritize precise measurement over regret.

prompt: An ad system has 40 creatives and new ones are added weekly; it should keep trying newcomers while favoring proven performers.
tells: keep trying newcomers while favoring proven performers
why: The explore–exploit trade-off with arms that keep changing.
trap: Re-running A/B tests for every new creative is too slow.
